topic.title: Model Editing and Preservation of Untargeted Knowledge
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Model editing changes selected facts or behaviors without rebuilding a model from scratch. This topic studies explicit edit memories, parameter updates, lifelong sequences of corrections, and concept removal. The main challenge is defining an edit’s intended scope while preserving unrelated behavior and avoiding interference as edits accumulate.
topic.whyItMatters: A correction should generalize to relevant paraphrases without spreading to unrelated questions. Sequential updates make this harder because individually successful edits can conflict. Evaluations therefore need to measure locality, retention, and composition, rather than only whether one edited prompt receives the desired answer.
topic.evolution: SERAC in 2022 stores edits in a retrieval-based memory and learns when to apply them across several language tasks. Later representatives introduce lifelong adaptors and memory mechanisms. Recent work examines theoretical limits of parameter editing; a 2026 diffusion-model method uses orthogonal transformations to separate concept erasure from preservation of broader generative geometry.
openQuestions: How can edit scope be specified and tested beyond a small set of paraphrases?
Which memory or parameter structures best prevent interference during long sequences of edits?
